verdict.rationale: Jitsu has its own headless automation path. jitsu-cli manages workspace configuration objects and is described as doing everything the UI does, and functions can be built and deployed from your own repo via `jitsu-cli init`/`deploy`. A public Management HTTP API also covers workspaces, destinations, connections, syncs and functions. The docs explicitly cover CI/headless environments, where you authenticate with a personal API key instead of the browser flow, and named API tokens with expiration are available. Missing for 10: a documented CI pipeline recipe for jitsu-cli (e.g., a GitHub Actions example), independent hands-on corroboration of running in CI, and a machine-readable OpenAPI spec at the probed paths (the probe returned 404, though docs claim one at docs.jitsu.com/api).
